My Story
My path into data science didn’t start with a laptop, it started in a remote tribal district in India, where I was working to improve sanitation conditions for communities in Dhar. What struck me wasn’t just the scale of the problem, but how much sharper our decisions became when we let data lead. Using visualisations to strategise where to target resources and time, we helped villagers gain access to something as fundamental as a toilet. That experience changed how I think about what data is actually for.
From there I joined SHEROES, a women-centred social platform, as a Product Manager, helping build and scale a community mobile application that gave women a safe space and a launchpad for their entrepreneurial journeys. Working at that intersection of people, product, and technology made me want to go deeper into the technical side. So I did an MSc in Applied Data Science and Statistics at the University of Exeter and haven’t looked back. My dissertation explored the evolution of evolutionary linguistics, sitting at an unlikely crossroads of data and language that I found fascinating.
I now work as a Data Scientist with the University of Southampton, building LLM-driven tools for NIHR’s research funding body NETSCC; automating and simplifying workflows while keeping the human firmly in the loop.

Outside of work
I love trying things I haven’t done before. Right now that means bouldering, swimming, knitting, and working my way through my book club’s reading list, currently on The Raven Scholar. I travel whenever I can, with a mix of adventure, relaxation, and getting genuinely lost in a new culture. The Norway trip that inspired the photo above was one of those.

title: Always Building
text:
Hi, I’m Poonam Brar, a Data Scientist at the University of Southampton, building AI/ML and data science solutions for NETSCC, NIHR that automate and simplify research workflows while keeping the human in the loop.
I hold an MSc in Applied Data Science and Statistics from the University of Exeter. I love working at the intersection of rigorous research and practical engineering turning messy, complex problems into something that actually works.
Right now I’m deepening my deep learning knowledge through fast.ai, and I’m always interested in conversations about AI in healthcare, research automation, or anything data-driven.
If you’d like to collaborate or just talk ideas, feel free to reach out.

title: Sustrans — National Cycle Network Accessibility
text:
The National Cycle Network spans thousands of miles across the UK, but not all of it is equally accessible. Sustrans — the charity behind the network — wanted to better understand where the barriers to access lie and how they could be addressed.
This project was completed as part of the Data Study Group at The Alan Turing Institute, working collaboratively with a team of data scientists.

title: Northern Power Grid — Energy Transition Analysis
text:
As the UK transitions to clean energy, grid operators need to know where to prioritise asset upgrades and which power generators are best suited for conversion to renewable sources. Northern Power Grid needed data-driven answers to both questions.
This project was completed as part of the Data Study Group at The Alan Turing Institute.

title: Northern Power Grid — Energy Transition Analysis
text:
As the UK transitions to clean energy, grid operators need to know where to prioritise asset upgrades and which power generators are best suited for conversion to renewable sources. Northern Power Grid needed data-driven answers to both questions.
This project was completed as part of the Data Study Group at The Alan Turing Institute.

title: Northern Power Grid — Energy Transition Analysis
text:
Approach
I analysed spatial and temporal patterns in power consumption and station capacity across the northern UK. To identify stations under the most strain, I applied Extreme Value Theory — a statistical technique for modelling the probability of rare but significant deviations from normal behaviour.
The outputs included visualisations of stations where asset upgrades are required and recommendations for which power generators should be prioritised for conversion to solar and wind.

title: Evolution of Evolutionary Linguistics
text: Evolutionary Linguistics is a field that sits at the crossroads of biology, cognitive science, and linguistics — but how has its research landscape actually evolved over time? With hundreds of papers spanning multiple disciplines, manually identifying the key themes and how they relate to each other would be near impossible.

title: Evolution of Evolutionary Linguistics
text: Evolutionary Linguistics is a field that sits at the crossroads of biology, cognitive science, and linguistics — but how has its research landscape actually evolved over time? With hundreds of papers spanning multiple disciplines, manually identifying the key themes and how they relate to each other would be near impossible.

title: Evolution of Evolutionary Linguistics
text:
Approach
I applied topic modelling to a corpus of 413 research papers to surface the dominant concepts driving the field. From there, I used network science to build a graph of causal relationships between those concepts — making it possible to see not just what the field is about, but how its ideas connect and cluster.
Community detection algorithms identified mathematically formed groups of concepts, which I then analysed for their significance and evolution over time.

title: Evolution of Evolutionary Linguistics
text:
Tools & Techniques

Topic modelling (LDA)
Network science — centrality measures, community detection
Python (NetworkX, Gensim, Matplotlib)
